title: Chrome new window fails with Always on top

judgment.rationale: The reported sequence is clear, but current source requests topmost status and the desired exception could conflict with the core feature.
evidence: On 0.75.1 a new Chrome window appears behind a Chrome window pinned with Always on Top, and the reporter expects access to the new window.
The original pinned window is intentionally topmost; the requested access behavior must be reconciled with that contract.

Always on Top sets HWND_TOPMOST on the selected window and removes it with HWND_NOTOPMOST: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/AlwaysOnTop/AlwaysOnTop/AlwaysOnTop.cpp.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported sequence is clear, but current source requests topmost status and the desired exception could conflict with the core feature.

proposed_fixes.title: Clarify access to new Chrome windows while pinned
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A normal new window appearing behind a topmost window may be expected Windows z-order behavior, not an implementation defect; a different policy would need explicit product agreement.
plan: Reproduce with a pinned Chrome window and compare an unrelated unpinned window.
Determine whether the new Chrome window is normally reachable by repositioning or task switching and document the expected topmost semantics.
Only if maintainers want different child-window behavior, design an explicit opt-in policy that preserves the pinned window's topmost contract and avoids promoting unrelated windows.
verification: Pinned windows retain their documented topmost behavior, and any approved access mechanism for new Chrome windows works without unexpected topmost promotion.

setup: Open a Chrome window and pin it with Always on Top.
steps: Open a new Chrome window from the pinned window.
